digest.en: Kallas faces a direct threat from Moscow that any EU role in Ukraine talks will collapse negotiations. Simultaneously, Shenzhen's summit reveals a widening tech divide as California investigates Nvidia's chip exports to China.
digest.hi: Bangladesh's minister's house in Dhaka was hit by a petrol bomb, igniting a blaze that spread beyond the compound. Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina ordered a rapid response, but the fire reached the neighboring residential area before containment.

articles.title: Russia says role for EU's Kallas in Ukraine talks with Moscow would lead to their collapse
articles.summary: Russia rejected EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas for Ukraine negotiations. Moscow's spokesperson called her unsuitable and anti-Russian. The Kremlin stated her involvement would cause talks to collapse immediately. Zakharova told a press briefing in Moscow that Kallas was totally unsuitable to take part in such talks and listed ‌a series of statements from Kallas which she ​said showed the EU official was anti-Russian.

articles.title: Hunger striker in ICE detention tells of force-feeding ordeal – and what made him crack
articles.summary: Cuban asylum seeker Luis Alejandro Cora Pérez ended a hunger strike in Texas. He described being force-fed through a tube after five days of resistance. The physical pain forced him to stop the protest. articles.title: Asian American women feel impact of Nvidia CEO affair scandal, 'spy' accusations
articles.summary: Asian American women in tech report anxiety over Nvidia CEO scandal. They fear renewed scrutiny and "spy" accusations will harm their careers. The incident highlights persistent stereotypes despite professional achievements. Asian American women working in tech, civil rights advocacy and academia have felt a sense of dread that this ordeal will diminish how their peers are viewed and treated in their workplaces.

articles.title: California investigates Nvidia over whether chip exports ended up in China
articles.summary: California Attorney General Rob Bonta subpoenaed Nvidia. The state investigates whether chip exports reached China despite restrictions. Officials suspect the company misled investors regarding compliance. articles.title: Pakistan Climate Minister arrives in Delhi to attend SCO Civilisations Dialogue Forum
articles.summary: Pakistan's climate minister arrived in Delhi for the SCO Civilisations Dialogue Forum. Prime Minister Modi will inaugurate the event at Purana Quila. Pakistan currently chairs the SCO Council of Heads of State. Pakistan is the current chair of the SCO Council of Heads of State (CHS) (SCO_CHS) for the period of 2026-27; the event, which will be inaugurated by PM Modi, will be held at Delhi’s iconic Purana Quila (Old Fort), a 16th Century fort built by Emperor Humayun.

articles.title: China’s research ships turning ocean science into undersea warfare
articles.summary: China is expanding dual-use oceanographic ship deployments across the Indo-Pacific to map seafloors and track submarines. These vessels operate under scientific cover while threatening undersea cables. The strategy extends Beijing's military reach beyond traditional naval assets. Under the cover of scientific research and deep-sea exploration, China is deploying dual-use survey vessels across the Indo-Pacific to map seafloors, track submarines, and threaten undersea cables, bolstering its military reach.

articles.title: Shenzhen summit opens door to great power peace dialogue
articles.summary: US, Chinese, and Russian presidents met in Shenzhen to issue a joint peace declaration. The four-point document calls for United Nations reform, increased petroleum product supplies, and limits on international court jurisdiction. The leaders also committed to dialogue on reducing nuclear risks. The presidents of the United States, China and Russia have issued a four-point peace declaration calling for United Nations (UN) reform, more refined petroleum products, limits on the jurisdiction of international courts and dialogue on reducing nuclear risks.

articles.title: Battle to control GPS and radio signals raises civilian safety concerns
articles.summary: GPS and radio signals are increasingly blocked or faked, endangering aid convoys, passenger jets, and cargo ships. Civilian safety is declining as these critical navigation systems become unreliable. The disruption affects both conflict zones and open ocean routes. From aid convoys in conflict zones to passenger jets and cargo ships far out at sea, safe journeys depend on GPS, satellite navigation and old-fashioned radio transmissions.

articles.title: Ambition goes missing as fossil fuel language drops from draft deal
articles.summary: The latest draft climate agreement for COP31 removed explicit language on phasing out fossil fuels. This deletion occurred as ministers and the Presidency attempted to bridge sharp differences before the summit's scheduled close. Civil society groups expressed serious concern over the missing commitment. The change signals a significant retreat in the text's ambition regarding energy transition. A cat named Ambition went missing again at COP31 on Thursday.

articles.title: A Blown Bridge, A Big Meeting, And A 'Ludicrous Fantasy'
articles.summary: Moscow issued unrealistic European security demands despite losing the Kerch Bridge. The bridge partially collapsed during recent strikes. A meeting of three presidents drew attention. Analysts question the substance of the negotiations. Moscow makes what an analyst called "completely unrealistic" demands about European security despite setbacks in its war on Ukraine -- including the partial destruction of the only bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea.

articles.title: In Shenzhen, great-power pageantry masks a hardening tech divide
articles.summary: Trump and Xi addressed APEC leaders in Shenzhen, contrasting Washington's deregulatory stance with its expanding tech export controls. The summit highlighted a widening technological divide between the two powers. Their speeches underscored the hardening split in global digital governance. Speaking in rapid succession at the APEC leaders’ summit in Shenzhen on Thursday morning, Donald Trump and Xi Jinping offered Pacific Rim economies a stark study in diplomatic contrast, highlighting the widening gulf between Washington’s deregulatory rhetoric and the extraterritorial reach of its technology controls.

articles.title: Awami League’s violent comeback bid affirms its ‘terrorist’ label
articles.summary: Armed attackers burned the home of Awami League lawmaker SM Zilany in Tungipara on November 17. They also set fire to the local police station. The violence followed a checkpoint operation and reinforced the party's designation as a terrorist organization. On November 17, armed attackers set fire to the residence of Bangladesh’s ruling party lawmaker SM Zilany in Tungipara, Gopalganj, the ancestral political stronghold of ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina’s family.

articles.title: Iranian Doctor Accused Of Spreading 'False Information' About Single Mothers
articles.summary: Iranian authorities opened a case against an obstetrician for spreading false information. She posted a video noting a rise in single mothers. The action signals a crackdown on discussions of social change within the country. An Iranian obstetrician posted a video online in which she said she's observed a growing number of single women having babies. Iranian authorities reacted by opening a case against her for allegedly spreading misinformation, suggesting an effort to suppress discussions of social change.

articles.title: Trump’s $23 billion battleship faces sinking odds
articles.summary: Trump’s $23 billion battleship proposal faces budget hurdles. Democrats are preparing to control Congress. Defense officials debate whether to fund a new capital ship or next-generation destroyers to counter China’s expanding naval fleet. As Democrats prepare to take over Congress and defense budget cuts loom, US President Donald Trump’s proposed battleship has sparked debate over whether to invest in a costly capital ship or next-generation destroyers to counter China’s growing fleet.

articles.title: Ukraine Wrecked Putin's Bridge. Now It Can Choke Russian Supplies To Crimea
articles.summary: Ukraine destroyed the $4 billion Crimean Bridge, cutting road traffic between the Russian mainland and the peninsula. The damage severely strains Moscow's ability to supply the Black Sea region. Kyiv's strike targets a key Kremlin infrastructure asset. For eight years, it’s stood as a symbol of the Kremlin’s claim to Crimea: a $4 billion bridge directly linking the Russian mainland with the Ukrainian peninsula.

articles.title: RFE/RL Visits Ukraine's Newly Liberated Territory After Operation Vivaldi
articles.summary: Ukraine's Third Army Corps liberated 16 settlements and 277 square kilometers in Donetsk during Operation Vivaldi. RFE/RL journalists visited the newly secured frontline positions. They retraced the specific paths taken by Ukrainian infantry and assault troops during the military campaign. Ukraine's Third Army Corps liberated 16 settlements and 277 square kilometers in the Donetsk region during Operation Vivaldi. RFE/RL visits the frontline positions and retraces the path of the Ukrainian infantry and assault troops who took part in the military campaign.

articles.title: COP31 deadlock persists as countries launch new ‘climate reality check’
articles.summary: COP31 delegates in Antalya launched a new global check on climate promise fulfillment. Ministers remain deadlocked over funding responsibilities and fossil fuel transition timelines. The core dispute centers on whether a greener future is just if poorer nations cannot afford the shift. With the clock running down at COP31 in Antalya, countries on Wednesday launched a new global check on whether climate promises are being kept, even as ministers remained deadlocked over some of the summit’s toughest questions: who pays, how fast the world moves away from fossil fuels and whether a greener future can be called “just” if poorer countries cannot afford it.

articles.title: EU's $50 Billion Funding Push For Ukraine Caught In Budget Crossfire
articles.summary: The European Commission proposed a 45 billion euro loan for Ukraine on November 18. The funds aim to cover the country's 2027 financial shortfall. The plan now faces significant delays due to internal budget disputes within the bloc. The European Commission is putting forward a new 45-billion-euro ($50 billion) loan proposal for Ukraine on November 18, to cover a large part of the financial shortfall the war-torn country is facing for 2027.

articles.title: Fears grow that US will put Nobel-winning judge under sanctions after Myanmar genocide ruling
articles.summary: The International Court of Justice is set to rule on Myanmar's genocide charges against the Rohingya. U. S. officials may sanction judges, including Nobel laureate Navi Pillay, if the ruling goes against the Myanmar government. articles.title: Diversifying funding was supposed to protect civil society: It did not
articles.summary: A survey of 195 organizations across 68 countries reveals that diversified funding strategies failed to protect civil society groups from the global aid retreat. The crisis extends beyond immediate financial shortfalls, indicating deeper structural vulnerabilities. Organizations that spent years building varied revenue streams are still facing severe operational challenges and instability. A survey of 195 organisations across more than 68 countries shows how the global aid retreat is hitting organizations that spent years building diverse funding streams.

articles.title: Tit-For-Tat US-Iran Attacks Persist As Peace Deal Remains Elusive
articles.summary: US and Iranian forces exchanged air strikes across the Middle East. Gulf nations warned residents about incoming projectiles. Regional mediators attempted to halt the conflict. The low-level fighting continued despite diplomatic efforts to secure a peace deal. US and Iranian forces exchanged tit-for-tat air strikes in the Middle East, while Gulf nations issued fresh warnings to residents amid threats of incoming projectiles as the currently low-level conflict continued to brew despite the efforts of regional mediators.

articles.title: Caribbean nations fear economic impact of shuttering citizenship program after EU threats
articles.summary: St Kitts and Nevis will end its citizenship-by-investment program. The decision follows European Union threats to revoke visa-free access for its citizens. Nevis premier Terrance Drew warned the move threatens the island economy and its ability to support vulnerable residents. St Kitts and Nevis to wind down citizenship-by-investment program after EU warns of end to visa-free accessThe decision by St Kitts and Nevis to end a lucrative programme offering citizenship to wealthy foreigners in exchange for investment threatens its economy and ability to support people in need, the premier of the island of Nevis has warned. On Friday, Terrance Drew, the prime minister of the.

articles.title: Civilian casualties in 2026 already far exceed previous years’ tolls
articles.summary: The UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine reported that 2026 civilian casualties already exceed all previous years since the February 2022 invasion. The toll has risen dramatically compared to prior periods. This marks the highest recorded civilian death rate of the conflict to date. This year has seen dramatically higher civilian casualties in Ukraine than any other year since the full-scale invasion of the eastern European country by Russia in February 2022, the UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine (HRMMU) said on Tuesday.

articles.title: Ebola cases double in DR Congo, chemical exposure starts before birth, Türk concern over EU-Rwanda
articles.summary: The World Health Organization reported that Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo have more than doubled in three months. Over 11,000 cases and 5,400 deaths are now confirmed. The outbreak spans 67 health zones across eight provinces. The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has more than doubled in three months, with more than 11,000 cases and 5,400 deaths now reported in 67 health zones across eight provinces, the head of the World Health Organization (WHO) said on Tuesday.

articles.title: The push to protect warming oceans reaches the negotiating table
articles.summary: Scientists and communities presented nature protection strategies at COP31. These included using seawater to identify marine life and applying Indigenous knowledge for wildfire prevention. Negotiators still struggle to bridge divisions over fossil fuels and climate finance funding gaps. From identifying marine life with a cup of seawater to drawing on Indigenous knowledge to prevent wildfires, scientists and communities showcased both cutting-edge and time-tested ways to protect nature at COP31 on Tuesday.

articles.summary: बिलावल भुट्टो-जरदारी ने सिंध के बंटवारे की कोशिशों पर सरकार को चेतावनी दी। उन्होंने कहा कि जबरदस्ती से यह फैसला थोपा गया तो 30 साल तक संकट बना रहेगा। पाकिस्तान पीपुल्स पार्टी के चेयरमैन बिलावल भुट्टो-जरदारी ने सिंध के बंटवारे की कोशिशों पर पाकिस्तान सरकार को चेतावनी दी है. उन्होंने कहा कि अगर जबरदस्ती या जनमत संग्रह के जरिए सिंध को बांटने का फैसला थोपा गया, तो हालात बिगड़ सकते हैं और इस आग को बुझाने में 30 साल लग सकते हैं.
